literature_name: Acetatifactor (genomes in this GTDB genus also carry the NCBI name Waltera)
name_note: Many genomes in this GTDB genus carry the NCBI names Waltera or Clostridium, so the GTDB genus is broader than the originally described Acetatifactor.

sentences.text: The genus Acetatifactor was proposed for strain CT-m2, which was cultured with selective agar media from the caecum of mice fed a high calorie diet.
That strain belongs to the Clostridium cluster XIV and is most closely related to members of the Lachnospiraceae, including Anaerostipes, Blautia, Butyrivibrio and Coprococcus.
It is a non-motile Gram-positive rod that does not form spores, grows under strictly anoxic conditions, and produces acetate and butyrate in reduced WCA broth.
Obligately anaerobic, Gram-stain-negative wavy rods assigned to the genus Waltera, a name carried by genomes GTDB places here, were isolated from faeces of healthy Japanese people.
